data.description:
The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes
on every Gerrit vote. Give it diverged-detection, and fix the deploy path so the change actually
reaches the box. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Its clone lives on an EBS-backed external volume (`docker-compose.yml:127`, `external: true`) cloned
once behind `if [ ! -d .git ]` (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:117`, itself nested inside
`if [ -n "${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]` at `:112`), so a redeploy does **not** converge it. It
writes a `code_review` ticket and auto-pushes on **every** vote (`voter.py:260-343`,
`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`) — event-driven, not scheduled, so pausing AWS *schedules* does not stop it.

This is **new code, not a predicate fix**: `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` currently does only
`git config user.email/user.name` (`:52-53`) then `run_ensures` (`:59`) — no fetch, no reset, no
ancestry test. Note its invocation at `Dockerfile.reviewbot:125` sits OUTSIDE the PAT block, so new
logic there runs even with the PAT unset.

**Chicken-and-egg:** `autodeploy.sh:186`'s rsync — which is what refreshes the box's copy of these
scripts — runs only when `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS` changed (`:55` =
`src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot pyproject.toml infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`).
A commit touching only these two scripts would never reach the box. So this must land in the **same
change** as an `src/rebar/` edit (A6-0a qualifies).

## Approach
1. Add diverged-detection to `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`: if `HEAD` is not an ancestor of
   `origin/tickets` and not strictly ahead, `fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets`. Safe because the
   bot never holds unpushed work (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`).
2. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh:55`'s `BOT_PATHS`, so future
   edits to it deploy at all.

Vote safety is already guaranteed and must not regress: `voter.py:698` records the vote **before**
`emit_code_review_artifact` (`:735`), and that call is wrapped in `except Exception` ->
`_artifact_emit_error` + `logger.warning` + `return None` (`:368-371`) — documented as "the vote is
already cast, so this never fails the review". A store failure cannot wedge the `LLM-Review` gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a clone diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared tip), the script re-converges it to
      `origin/tickets` and leaves no local commits. Tier: **shell integration** against two real
      temporary repos.
- [ ] Given an up-to-date or merely-behind clone, the script makes **no** destructive change
      (negative control). Tier: **shell integration**.
- [ ] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the new logic still executes (it sits outside the PAT
      block). Tier: **shell integration** with the env var unset.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh`'s `BOT_PATHS`. Verify:
      grep assertion in a test.
- [ ] A rebar store write failure inside the bot still leaves the vote cast (regression guard). Tier:
      **unit** on `emit_code_review_artifact` with an injected store failure.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a (and must ship in the same change as an `src/rebar/` edit).
data.title: A6-0b: make the review-bot's tickets clone self-converge, and fix its deploy trigger
